title: Claude Code Dispatch: 10x Your Context Window

slides.text:
Your Claude Code session has a <accent>context window limit</accent>.

Every file read, every search, every tool call eats into it.

What if you could <accent>10x your effective context</accent> by turning your session into a lightweight orchestrator?

slides.heading: The <accent>Problem</accent>
before: Context fills up fast with sequential tasks
Session slows down as context grows
You restart and lose all progress
after: Each task gets a fresh context window

slides.heading: Install in <accent>10 Seconds</accent>
slides.body:
One command.
Global or project-level.
No config needed.

terminal.text: ✓ Available models detected: claude, gpt, gemini

slides.heading: Dispatch <accent>Your First Task</accent>
slides.body:
Name the model.
Describe the task.
That's it.

terminal.text: claude> /dispatch use opus to review this PR for edge cases
→ Your session is free. Keep working.
claude> /dispatch use sonnet to write integration tests

slides.heading: Workers Can <accent>Ask Questions</accent>
slides.body:
Workers don't fail silently.
They ask you for clarity.
You answer. They continue.
No context lost.

terminal.text: Q: Should I include auth edge cases
in the PR review, or just the
claude> Include both. Auth is critical.

slides.heading: Why This Is <accent>Powerful</accent>
items: 10x effective context — each worker gets a fresh window
Non-blocking — your session stays free while workers run
Multi-model — mix Claude, GPT, Gemini per task
Interactive — workers ask questions, you answer, no restart
Zero config — auto-detects models on first run

slides.heading: Mix <accent>Models</accent> Per Task
slides.body:
Use the right model
for the right job.
All from one session.

terminal.text: claude> /dispatch use opus to architect the database schema
claude> /dispatch use sonnet to write unit tests
claude> /dispatch use gpt-5.3 to refactor config parser

slides.text:
Stop filling one context window with everything.
Start orchestrating many.
